subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should memory status be resolved by live gateway runtime health, by local passive plugin status, or is current `not checked` output sufficient for this issue?
rationale: Current main avoids the old wording but does not implement the requested live-runtime health signal, while the open conflicting fork PR and broader related issue need an owner decision about the permanent status boundary.

options.title: Use the broader live-gateway contract
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 the canonical implementation path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Revive the fork PR
options.body: Ask the fork PR author to rebase, resolve conflicts, and prove human plus JSON status against a real external memory plugin without local plugin side effects.

options.title: Accept current `not checked` behavior
options.body: Declare the current softened status wording sufficient, close the conflicting fork PR, and close this issue only with explicit release/source evidence.

recommendation.title: Use the broader live-gateway contract
recommendation.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 the canonical implementation path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-tree blame places the active status, doctor, and memory-runtime surfaces under Vincent Koc's work.
